segment_text: b) MedQuist shall provide CBay with the billing data necessary for CBay to generate an invoice for the work performed by MedQuist to a Client Facility under this Agreement. CBay will in turn generate an invoice to Client Facility consistent with the billing data from MedQuist within three (3) calendar days of receipt of the billing data from MedQuist.

THIS IS THE FIRST ITEM IN THE SET WHERE A MISSING REGISTRY WAS LOAD-BEARING ON A SCORED CLAUSE. Batch 4 drafted three E08 items with no E08 registry, but none of them turned on it -- E08-02 and E08-04 are underspecified on an ABSENT obligee, E08-03 on trigger 3. Recorded so the precedent is not read as 'a document may be annotated without a registry'; it is 'no earlier item happened to depend on one'.

OBLIGEE = 'CBay' BY THE DATIVE, AND SECTION 3.5.2 CUTS AGAINST THE PURPOSE CLAUSE HERE RATHER THAN SUPPLYING IT. Section 3.5.2's condition 1 is decisive: 'provide CBay with the billing data' already names the party owed, so the trailing 'for CBay to generate an invoice' is the case that section's own text calls out -- it 'adds nothing and is not the basis'. THE CONTRAST WITH C04-08 IS WORTH STATING because the two items look alike: there no dative existed, so section 3.5.2's carve-in did the work and supplied 'Miltenyi' from a 'for the purposes of assisting X' clause. Same rule, opposite half, opposite direction.

CONDITIONS EMPTY -- 'necessary for CBay to generate an invoice for the work performed by MedQuist to a Client Facility under this Agreement' is OBJECT SCOPE, not a condition. Section 3.8.2's removal test (F8): delete the phrase and the duty applies in exactly the same circumstances; only the set of data it covers broadens. That is the section's own worked shape, and the extraction prompt asks for condition_raws as "'if'-type conditional phrases", which this is not.

ACTION: 'provide' is the literal verb, so section 8.8's genuine-gap class does not fire at all and no action_not_in_taxonomy is owed. DELIVER and REPORT are the defensible siblings -- section 3.4's own motivating example is 'submit a compliance report' with PROVIDE and REPORT both defensible, and batch 4's C04-08 carries this exact triple. DISCLOSE was CONSIDERED AND DECLINED: in this corpus it carries a confidentiality-revelation sense, not the furnishing of a contracted deliverable, so admitting it would start stretching the set toward the 'stops measuring whether extraction identified the action at all' failure section 8.8 names.

OBJECT_CLASS. Head noun of the object phrase ('the billing data necessary for...') is 'data', so 'data' is carried as the head-only member section 3.6's v0.58 forward rule requires of every item from batch 4 onward -- and it is the head noun OF THE OBJECT PHRASE, which is the bound C04-03's counter-example exists to enforce, not merely some 1-token label present in the span. Section 3.6 enum 1's two nominal anchors are the data itself and the invoice it feeds, hence invoice_data / invoicing_data. SECTION 3.6.1 AND 3.6.2 BOTH CLEAR: no member restates the action (PROVIDE) or either party (MedQuist, CBay), and 'billing_' names the data's kind rather than the duty type. 'data_provision' was deliberately NOT authored -- it would restate PROVIDE.

SPAN INCLUDES THE TRAILING PERIOD, per the measured gold convention (section 7.1's fourth finding: 19 of 31 matched items differ from the cold annotator only by a trailing '.', gold inclusive, zero the other way) and batch 4's C04-08.
